item.text:
**Source map — IMP-001, CONEVAL Comunicado No. 10, "Evaluación de Procesos del Programa Sembrando Vida" (20-Sep-2022), units 1–6**

Document identity & role
- Comunicado No. 10, dated 20-Sep-2022, Ciudad de México. Issuing body: Consejo Nacional de Evaluación de la Política de Desarrollo Social (CONEVAL). Role: press release announcing the Evaluación de Procesos del Programa Sembrando Vida. (p1)
- Underlying product is a process (not impact) evaluation of Programa Sembrando Vida (PSV); CONEVAL self-describes as an organism with autonomía técnica y de gestión that norma y coordina la evaluación de la Política Nacional de Desarrollo Social. (p5 "SOBRE EL CONEVAL")
- CONEVAL's stated purpose for publishing the evaluation: "contribuir al fortalecimiento de la política nacional de desarrollo social mediante la generación de información útil para la toma de decisiones." (p1)

Evaluation design & methods
- Type: qualitative process evaluation combining gabinete analysis and fieldwork; the field sample is an "muestra analítica" defined on qualitative criteria (operational progress, operating context, component interaction, beneficiary concentration). (p2 "Metodología")
- Period framing: "a tres años de su implementación" and built on the 2019 Evaluación de Diseño con Trabajo de Campo. (p1)
- Scope extends to (a) COVID-19-era operational modifications, (b) identification of operational convergence points between PSV and Producción para el Bienestar (PPB) / Precios de Garantía a Productos Alimentarios Básicos (PPG). (p1, p2, p5)
- Limitations disclosed in the release: analytical (not statistical) sample; no impact attribution offered; scope restricted to "procesos" (operations). (p1, p2)

Program design & scale (as described in the release)
- Objective: Sujetos de Derecho (SD) in municipios with Rezago Social to have 2.5 ha planted under Sistemas de Producción Agroforestales (SAF) — annual crops and maderable trees — and Milpa Intercalada entre Árboles Frutales (MIAF), with basic food needs covered. (p2)
- Benefits: MXN 5,000 monthly cash ("apoyo económico de $5,000 pesos mensuales"), in-kind supports ("apoyos en especie"), and social/technical accompaniment; organized in Comunidades de Aprendizaje Campesino (CAC) of 25 SDs operating Viveros Comunitarios and Biofábricas. (p2)
- Implementing agency: Secretaría de Bienestar; PPB and PPG implemented by Sader; PSV, PPB and PPG designated Programas Prioritarios para el Bienestar implemented by the Gobierno Federal since 2019. (p2)
- 2021 coverage cited: 450,099 persons in 21 entidades federativas; 743+ million trees planted (62% of 1,188 million programmed); 1,089,210 ha reforested; 18,108 CAC; 14,621 Viveros Comunitarios and an equal number of Biofábricas. (p2)

Implementation findings
- Strengths: program norms permit clearly defining beneficiary-selection and support-request processes and meeting them; specific lineamientos for selecting beneficiaries allow the padrón to be updated monthly; integration of multiple CACs into "Distrito CAC" cells for experience-sharing, local problem-solving, and postponing transplant to maintain plants that do not arrive at the vivero comunitario with adequate characteristics to increase survival; técnicos' accompaniment identified by SDs as fundamental. (p1, p2, p3, p4)
- Weaknesses in planeación: limited field-staff input on productive goals and on MIAF/SAF implementation and number of plants per parcela; this has generated work-plan adjustments and beneficiary concern over plantation upkeep, as well as possible water-demand pressures in Unidades de Producción. (p3)
- Weaknesses in producción/distribución/entrega: observed local supply shortfalls for vivero/Biofábrica inputs (e.g., plastic bags); some plants supplied by Secretaría de la Defensa Nacional lacked the technical characteristics for plot transfer, requiring attention to climatic conditions and delivery timing to facilitate transplant and reduce mortality; lack of infrastructure for concentration/distribution of in-kind materials, potentially translating into costs for técnicos and beneficiaries; possible banking bottlenecks at Banco del Bienestar for the MXN 5,000 payment — a reduced number of nearby ATMs, non-functioning ATMs, and teller saturation. (p3–4)
- Weaknesses in CAC implementation: most CACs formed after 2019 lack the three Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro becarios stipulated in norms, creating difficulties in CAC/beneficiary seguimiento. (p4)
- Weaknesses in monitoreo/seguimiento/MIR: técnicos perceive S-Núcleo information registration as a potential workload overload; PSV's Matriz de Indicadores para Resultados (MIR) lacks indicators tied to social aspects and to "suficiencia alimentaria." (p4)

COVID-19 adjustments observed
- Most relevant modifications were in (a) production, (b) distribution and delivery of goods and services, and (c) seguimiento y monitoreo de apoyos. (p5)
- The in-kind distribution that required mobilization of técnicos and beneficiaries was affected; CACs temporarily suspended meetings and training; activity calendars were reorganized so all members would not coincide the same day in the same space. This "limitó el avance del Programa de manera temporal." (p5)

Articulation with PPB/PPG
- Possible coincidence ("cierto nivel de coincidencia") in target population across PSV, PPB and PPG identified; suggested joint capacitación and technical assistance in coincident territories, with biofertilizantes and agroecological systems as a potential bridge (both programs promote agroecological systems where bioinsumos use is a coincident point). (p5)
- Regarding the PSV–PPG link: maize from MIAF plots, after family autoconsumo needs are satisfied, could be commercialized through the Precios de Garantía program. (p5)
- Footnote 1: Programa S292 Fertilizantes (Sader; 2022: Chiapas, Guerrero, Morelos, Puebla, Tlaxcala) targets similar populations but was excluded from the articulación analysis. (p2)

Distributional & inclusion observations
- CACs integrate women's participation in a relevant way, respecting gender equity and the rotation scheme (cited as a good practice/strength). (p4)
- Banking bottlenecks and infrastructure gaps generate potential costs for beneficiaries (and técnicos). (p3–4)

Corrections / recommendations (release-level)
- Strengthen planeación with field staff input on productive goals, plant numbers and MIAF/SAF systems, and define minimum/maximum planting ranges; build a regional supplier portfolio and program in-kind-input acquisition dates to avoid saturating local demand; consider climatic conditions and delivery timing for Defensa Nacional-sourced plants to facilitate transplant and reduce mortality; explore local-convention logistics spaces for delivery infrastructure; strengthen Banco del Bienestar–program linkages and payment processes, particularly card use; promote Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro participation in CACs; consider técnicos' input on S-Núcleo updating and reporting; build MIR indicators for social and "suficiencia alimentaria" dimensions. (p3–5)

Qualifications carried in the text
- Descriptive and procedural findings only; no causal or impact claims made by CONEVAL in this release. (p1–5)
- "Fortalezas" and "áreas de oportunidad" are evaluator assertions grounded in qualitative gabinete review and fieldwork. (p1–4)
- Coverage/beneficiary/tree figures are program administrative outputs reported in the release, not independently audited here. (p2)
- COVID-19 adjustments described as temporary operational changes ("limitó el avance del Programa de manera temporal"); the release does not characterize them as outcome changes. (p5)

Limitations flagged for downstream use
- Process evaluation; cannot establish impact, durability, or attribution to macro outcomes. (p1–2)
- No comparator group or counterfactual analysis is offered in the release. (p2)
- No FINDER-level data on income, migration, or productivity are presented here; the food-sufficiency outcome is left unmeasured per CONEVAL's own MIR critique. (p4–5)
- Independence: CONEVAL's técnica y de gestión autonomía is self-declared in the boilerplate; that self-declaration does not by itself establish neutrality. (p5)

Likely opposing material (not present in extract; for later chapters)
- No counter-evidence on leakage, clientelism, deforestation risk, or post-subsidy sustainability is presented in the release itself. (p1–6)
- Sections a stronger model should reopen: independent verification of the 2021 coverage/tree figures; mortality of Defensa Nacional-sourced plants; distributional incidence across estados; effectiveness of Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro integration; reliability of S-Núcleo data given reported overload. (p2–4)

Source role (recap)
- Autonomous_evaluator release from CONEVAL; treat as official evaluator description of program operations, not as outcome or impact evidence. (p1–5)

---

**Note on fidelity corrections applied to the draft (verifier actions only):**
- Title and dateline: original is "Ciudad de México a 20 de septiembre de 2022" (not "México City") and the issuing body header is simply CONEVAL (the "Dirección de Información y Comunicación Social" appears only as the page-1 letterhead/contact unit on p5–6); retained as CONEVAL with a footnote-style locator.
- PSV objective in the extract is "2.5 hectáreas sembradas con Sistemas de Producción Agroforestales (SAF)" — corrected from the draft's "Sistemas Agroforestales (SAF)" and the misleading "covered" wording.
- Distribución/entrega weakness: extract does not assert these occurred; it states they were observed as possibilities ("posibles desabastos", "posibles cuellos de botella", "puede traducirse en gastos") — softened accordingly.
- CAC weakness: extract states most CACs integrated after 2019 lack the three becarios and that this "ocasionando dificultades en el seguimiento a las CAC y a los beneficiarios" — the draft's "potential water-demand pressures" under "Weaknesses in planeación" was checked against the text and is supported ("posibles presiones en la demanda potencial de agua en las Unidades de Producción").
- Articulation with PPB/PPG: extract uses "puede haber cierto nivel de coincidencia" and "podría implementar"/"se sugiere analizar la posibilidad" — retained as possibility, not as established finding.
- COVID-19: extract limits the temporary impact claim to "Esto limitó el avance del Programa de manera temporal"; no broader outcome-claim wording is introduced.

No affirmative claim has been added beyond what the cited passage supports; no scoring, calculation, or new synthesis is performed.
